evidence_used: Order created 13:12:58 and auto-cancelled at 14:13:00 by the 60-min hold stock limit; payment captured later at 14:13:41. The 504s were real but once webhooks got through at 14:15 the plugin refused to update because the order was already cancelled (telemetry 'not in pending/failed state (cancelled)'), and cron skipped it too. The timeout was not the reason it stayed unpaid.
fix: Manually move order 5521 back to processing and mark it paid against pay_Q1aK7mT3vR9pLz (check stock). Raise or disable WooCommerce hold stock minutes so it exceeds the checkout window. Separately consider more PHP workers for sale traffic.

evidence_used: Every webhook since 10:02 returned 403 Forbidden in ~40ms with a generic HTML page, which is a firewall block, not PHP. Wordfence has rate limiting and no-user-agent blocking on. The child theme fatal error is at 12:47, after webhooks had already been failing for nearly 3 hours, and it sits in the thank-you page hook, not the webhook handler. Cron saw no pending webhooks because none reached the site.
fix: Allowlist the Razorpay webhook endpoint / Razorpay IPs in Wordfence (or exempt the route from rate limiting and UA blocking), then mark order 18834 paid against pay_Q2cH5nV8kD1sYw. Fix the child theme functions.php call separately since it breaks the thank-you page.

evidence_used: Razorpay sent webhooks 2s after capture (14:10:07); the site returned 504 after 30s on each try during the 14:00-15:00 flash sale on a 1-worker shared plan. Razorpay retried at 14:15 and 14:50; the 14:50 retry got a 200 and the order moved to processing immediately. So delivery was not delayed by Razorpay; the site could not respond.
fix: No action on order 9047 (now processing). Add PHP workers / upgrade hosting or cache-exclude and lighten the webhook path before sales; set up a server cron so the plugin's fallback check runs.

evidence_used: Both webhooks got 200 in under 200ms, yet the order is still pending 14 hours later and there is no plugin telemetry at all. The site moved hosts and installed LiteSpeed Cache the day before, so a cached 200 or a webhook URL pointing at the old host is plausible, but nothing confirms which.
fix: Mark order 2214 paid manually against pay_Q4gN9xC3aJ5uRd. Ask the merchant to confirm the webhook URL resolves to the new host, exclude the Razorpay webhook endpoint from LiteSpeed Cache, enable plugin debug logging, and share server access logs for 19:21:32-33 on 2026-10-10.
